what_happened: While you were on a 19-minute call with a number calling itself "T-Mobile Support", someone asked you to turn off Port Out Protection and create a transfer PIN.
why_we_stepped_in: That number couldn't be verified and had never contacted you before, and turning off protection during a call like this is a common scam pattern.
confidence_text: We're fairly confident this was a scam, but not certain.
what_we_did: Turned Port Out Protection back on
Held your transfer PIN for 24 hours so it can't be used
next_steps: Nothing else is needed. Your number is safe.
If you shared bank details on that call, call your bank using the number on your card.
Reply REPORT and we'll fill in an FTC report for you.
spot_it_next_time: T-Mobile will never call and ask you to turn off protection or read out a PIN or code.
data_we_looked_at: When your call started and whether the number was verified
Account changes made during that call
Whether this was your usual device and area

replies.meaning: Safely release the hold (after the call, with a check)
